raw_response: Banks reported that the FDIC special assessment significantly impacted their expense figures, often requiring adjustments to show underlying trends. In Q4 2023, Bank of America noted a large FDIC special assessment charge in its reported expenses, though this was partially offset by a roughly $300 million release of prior period accruals for the same assessment; excluding the charge, expenses increased due to other factors like higher incentives and investments. In Q1 2024, Bank of America reported total expenses of $17.2 billion including the FDIC assessment, which adjusted down to $16.5 billion when excluding it. Similarly, Fifth Third Bancorp incorporated the FDIC insurance assessment rate change into its full-year expense outlook for 2023, noting that core expenses would have been lower (up less than 3%) if excluding the FDIC assessment and other specific items. Wells Fargo attributed part of the year-to-date increase in operating losses in the first half of 2024 to the FDIC expense, alongside remediation costs and variable expenses.
